status: COMPLETE — steps 1-5 of 5 done. This file accumulates findings AS THEY OCCUR rather than being written at the close, so a finding is durable at the moment it is made and cannot be smoothed over by what comes after.

steps_done.1: `MeasurementProtocol` — the declarations the standing intent's digests stand for, self-checking against the intent AND against a key, carried by the record as an optional fact.
steps_done.2: `MeasurementRequest` — construct-or-refuse, attesting to its key by resolving the candidate map over the record's own surface under the record's own layout policy.
steps_done.3: `PreparedExperiment::of(snapshot)` — four answers, derived from the record and nothing else.
steps_done.4: The executor seam — `ExperimentExecutor` selected by procedure name, `ArtifactLocator` for where things are, `DeclaredArtifacts` as the first locator, and a procedure-neutral `Observed`.
steps_done.5: `TeacherForcedExecutor` — the first registered procedure, as an adapter over the existing runner.

predictions_scored.P1: MET. One optional `SearchConfig::protocol` field, refused by name when absent, with no change to `MeasurementKey`, `MeasurementIntent` or `NextExperiment` and no digest moved. The whole read path still answers on a record that carries no protocol — asserted by `a_record_that_names_its_protocol_only_by_digest_refuses_and_says_so`, which calls `next_experiment` successfully on the same record it then fails to prepare.
predictions_scored.P2: MET, and stronger than forecast. `derived_key` re-derives the four-part key from the request alone with NO arguments, because the layout policy is resolved from the name the request carries. The forecast assumed a layout would have to be passed in.
predictions_scored.P3: MET. No type in `actuate/` mentions a device, backend, kernel, lowering target or store id. The one place a container path appears is `ArtifactLocator`, and it appears as a return value.
predictions_scored.P4: MET, and each of the three is observably different from the adapter's default rather than merely sourced differently — `kimi-logit-balanced-v1` vs `kimi-logit-v3`, 256 vs 32 sequences, `exp-<digest>` vs `q2a`.
predictions_scored.P5: MET, with one honest narrowing recorded as ACT1-N3: two of the three artifacts are checked and the third cannot be, and the module says which.
predictions_scored.P6: MET. Nothing in `actuate/` writes to `SearchFacts`; `preparing_twice_gives_the_same_request_and_changes_nothing` asserts the registry is untouched after two preparations.

ACT1-N1.title: The applied set — the only fact that says HOW a state is reached — was dropped between `Candidate` and `Assessment`.
ACT1-N1.against: The freeze's B2, which said the state was the one recoverable part of a key.
ACT1-N1.evidence: `Candidate::applied` exists and `Assessment::of` did not copy it, so `MeasurementOpportunity` — what `next_experiment` returns — carried `child_state` (a one-way digest) and no route to it. Building the overlay needs the MAP, and the map is `base_map` plus an applied set.
ACT1-N1.consequence: B2 was right that the state is recoverable IN PRINCIPLE and wrong that the selection carried what recovery needs. The selected experiment was nameable and not performable, and nothing failed — because nothing had ever tried to build one.
ACT1-N1.resolution: `Assessment` carries `applied`, copied from the candidate, never re-derived from the action. It is an ingredient like every other field on that type, and the type is not serialised, so the stored-form anti-cheat is unaffected.
ACT1-N1.scored: Movement inside the wave's shape, not a redesign. It is the cheapest possible instance of the wave's whole thesis: a read path can look complete while carrying nothing an actuator can use, and only trying to actuate it finds out.

ACT1-N2.title: The gate gap 5a-0 named is wider than a wrong default — a build can REDEFINE a gate the record names.
ACT1-N2.observed: `gate_by_id` resolves four gates by id, and `SearchConfig::gate` stores a whole `QualityGate` with its thresholds. Those are two authorities for one name. A record carrying `kimi-logit-balanced-v1` with the thresholds of the day it was written, replayed against a build whose `kimi_logit_balanced_v1()` has moved, would be JUDGED under the current definition while claiming the recorded one.
ACT1-N2.why_it_is_not_hypothetical: `quality.rs` documents exactly this movement for v1 to v3: 'v3 sets none, because the counts were measured and found unable to separate a coin flip from an overturned decision'. Gates in this programme change, and they change by having a new id — but nothing enforced that, and the `debug_assert_eq!` inside `gate_by_id` only checks that a gate answers to its own name, not that the record agrees with it.
ACT1-N2.resolution: `RequestRefusal::GateRedefined`. Preparation resolves the record's gate id and refuses unless the resolved gate EQUALS the one the record carries. Caught before the run rather than reported after it by `Inadmissible::GateMismatch`, which could only ever say so once the instrument time had been spent.
ACT1-N2.scored: An unforecast refusal, found by writing the mapping rather than by reasoning about it. It is the same class as the `NullArmNotZero` variant the 5a-0b conservation inventory found by walking the harness assertion by assertion.

ACT1-N3.title: Two of the three located artifacts can be checked against the record; the third cannot, and it is the one that matters most.
ACT1-N3.checkable: A container states its own identity (`read_source_identity`), and a corpus's `manifest.json` digests to the input the bank id was computed over. Both are verified on every answer, not at registration, because either can be replaced under a path between one experiment and the next.
ACT1-N3.not_checkable_here: A compiled overlay carries no identity a locator can read. Establishing that the bytes on disk present the state the key names means opening them under the same layout and accounting authority the record declares — the executor's bind step, and for admissibility stage 6's.
ACT1-N3.handling: Recorded rather than papered over: `candidate` looks up by state id and refuses `NotBuilt` when absent, and `artifacts.rs` says in its own module doc which of the three it has verified and which it has not. A locator that returned an overlay path with an implied claim of correctness would be the presence-implies-trust failure ATTESTATION-1 named one plane down.
ACT1-N3.consequence_for_stage_6: The 'does this artifact constitute the measurement named by this key' question therefore has a real job to do at ingestion and is not a formality the bridge already answered.

ACT1-N4.title: The seam needs its own falsifier, distinct from the request's.
ACT1-N4.observed: The wave's headline falsifier is about PREPARATION — a request may not misstate its experiment. Writing the registry made it obvious that the guarantee stops at the trait boundary: an executor is free to return an observation of anything, and a bridge that carefully constructed a truthful request and then accepted an answer about a different state would have bought nothing.
ACT1-N4.resolution: `Observed` carries the key it is an observation OF, and `ExecutorRegistry::execute` refuses `ObservedAnotherExperiment` when that is not the key it handed over. The test asserts BOTH directions — a lying stub refused, an honest one accepted — because a check that refuses everything is indistinguishable from a check that works.
ACT1-N4.scored: Not in the freeze. Recorded as an addition the freeze should have anticipated: every place an identity crosses an abstraction boundary in this programme has needed the same check, and this was the first boundary where the identity left the crate's own control.
ACT1-N4.promotion: This check belongs to the optimizer as a whole rather than to 5b. The executor sits outside the deterministic search kernel, so its first obligation is 'I measured the experiment you authorised' before anyone considers what number it produced. Owed: promotion from an ordinary test to a permanent optimizer invariant, in a contract index of its own (OPT-CONTRACT-1) rather than appended to the frozen REPRESENT/accounting v1 index, which defines itself as nine contracts and whose checker is hard-coded to that file.

ACT1-N5.title: `MeasurementProtocol::procedure` and `InstrumentSemantics::procedure` are two claims in two namespaces, and no mapping between them has been earned.
ACT1-N5.the_two: `q2a-teacher-forced/baseline-vs-overlay` is what a reading MEANS and is inside the instrument digest. `teacher-forced-two-arm/v1` is what this build must PERFORM and is in no digest.
ACT1-N5.decision: They are separate fields with NO cross-check asserted. Inventing one — 'a q2a instrument implies the teacher-forced procedure' — would be a claim about instruments this programme has no evidence for, and it would be invisible the first time it was wrong.
ACT1-N5.guard: `the_executable_procedure_is_not_the_instrument_s_procedure` asserts that renaming what the build performs does not move the instrument digest, so the independence is a tested property rather than an accident.
ACT1-N5.when_this_should_change: When a second procedure exists and something has to decide which one an instrument's declared procedure implies. That is a registration with its own evidence, not a string comparison.

ACT1-N6.title: `RequestRefusal::UnresolvableLayout` is unreachable through the record-derived path, and is kept anyway.
ACT1-N6.observed: `PreparedExperiment::of` calls `next_experiment`, which builds a price table, which resolves the layout policy first. A record naming a policy this build lacks therefore answers `NotSelectable` and never reaches preparation.
ACT1-N6.why_kept: It IS reachable through `MeasurementRequest::of`, which a caller holding several already-authorised keys — an `ExecutionBatch` — uses directly. A refusal that only one of two doors can produce is still a refusal that door needs.
ACT1-N6.guard: `a_layout_policy_this_build_does_not_implement_is_refused_by_name` goes through that door explicitly and says in its own comment why it does not use the other one, so a later reader does not 'simplify' it into a test that silently asserts `NotSelectable` instead.

ACT1-N7.title: The Metal arm of the only registered executor compiles and has never run.
ACT1-N7.observed: `TeacherForcedExecutor::execute` has two cfg arms. The non-Metal one is tested — it instructs, then refuses with the backend's own message. The Metal one reaches `measure::run` and has no witness, because running it needs a real container, a real exported corpus and a compiled overlay at once, and none of those is a fixture.
ACT1-N7.why_it_is_recorded_rather_than_fixed: Earning it inside this wave would mean acquiring a real end-to-end measurement, which broadens a clean architectural rung for the wrong reason. It belongs to stage 6's evidence programme: the moment a real observation exists is exactly when the question 'does this deserve to become scientific state' is being asked.
ACT1-N7.the_reading_to_avoid: `the executor returned the requested key` does NOT mean `the candidate bytes were independently proven to present the state that key names`. ACT1-N3 already says why — a compiled overlay carries no identity a locator can read — but the seam's key check makes the stronger reading tempting, so `teacher_forced.rs` now states the compiled/witnessed split in its own module doc.
ACT1-N7.scored: A stated limit, not a finding against the design. The architecture is unchanged; only the evidentiary boundary is made unmistakable.

ACT1-N8.title: The coverage gate found that a third of the wave's refusals had never been rendered.
ACT1-N8.observed: `check_coverage_policy.py` failed four of the six new files on the 90%-per-file default: executor.rs 76.36%, teacher_forced.rs 81.63%, request.rs 86.36%, artifacts.rs 87.14%. Reproduced locally to the decimal.
ACT1-N8.what_it_actually_caught: Almost every uncovered line was a `Display` arm or a refusal branch nothing triggered — `NotHeld` for a locator that holds nothing, `NotInstructable` for a bank declaring no samples, `UnresolvableGate` for a gate this build never heard of, and the `Ranked` and `Exhausted` arms of preparation. The tests pattern-matched refusal VARIANTS and only rarely asserted their MESSAGES.
ACT1-N8.why_that_is_not_a_coverage_technicality: In this programme a refusal is contract surface, not a log line. `NotBuilt` promises to name the map to build; `NoSuchProcedure` promises to name what IS implemented; `StateMismatch` promises both digests. A variant that holds those facts and renders a message without them is the same dead end as no refusal at all, and nothing had checked.
ACT1-N8.resolution: A dedicated `refusals` test module asserting, for every arm of all three refusal types, that the rendered message carries the facts the variant holds. The `must_say` matches are exhaustive, so a new variant cannot be added without deciding what its message must say. Plus real triggers for the five untested branches. NO baseline entry was added: the policy file states the per-file list is existing debt that should only ratchet upward, and new code claiming an exemption on its first day is exactly what that sentence forbids.
ACT1-N8.also_removed: `From<MeasurementRefusal> for ExecutionRefusal` had no caller — both construction sites name the variant explicitly. Deleted rather than covered, in the same spirit as Ruling 1's absent fourth prune: present-and-unused is worse than absent.
ACT1-N8.residue_stated: Eight lines in `request.rs` remain uncovered and are unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION: the error arms of `attests_to_its_key`, which cannot fire while `MeasurementRequest::of` is the only constructor. They exist for a request that has travelled — over a queue, out of a file — and become reachable, and testable, the day the type gains serde. That is likely to be stage 6's problem, and the arms are kept rather than deleted for it.
ACT1-N8.scored: An unforecast finding from a gate rather than from a reviewer, and the reason the gate is set per-file rather than per-crate: the crate total was never in danger.

ACT1-N9.title: Mutation testing found the residue of the coverage fix: three survivors where a line RAN and nothing depended on what it produced.
ACT1-N9.observed: `cargo-mutants` on the diff reported three MISSED mutants, all in `actuate/artifacts.rs`: `short() -> ""`, `short() -> "xyzzy"`, and `DeclaredArtifacts::overlay_for -> None`. All three files were at or above the coverage floor by then.
ACT1-N9.the_distinction_that_matters: Line coverage proved those lines executed. The mutants proved no assertion depended on what they produced. The two are different claims, and ACT1-N8's fix bought the first without the second.
ACT1-N9.why_it_landed_exactly_there: `short` has ONE production use: the digest pair inside the corpus-mismatch `detail` string. `refusals.rs` asserts that each refusal TYPE renders the fields its variant holds — but this refusal's detail is COMPOSED AT THE CALL SITE in `artifacts.rs`, so the type-level contract never reached it. The test that triggered the refusal matched the variant and never read the message.
ACT1-N9.what_it_refines_in_contract_5: Proving a refusal type renders its fields is not sufficient. Where a refusal's actionable facts are assembled by the CONSTRUCTION SITE into a free-text field, that site needs its own witness. The type contract and the construction contract are two obligations, and only the first was frozen.
ACT1-N9.resolution: The corpus-mismatch test now asserts the detail names BOTH digests, and `overlay_for` is asserted in the positive direction as well as the negative — a mutant returning `None` unconditionally survived because only the absent case was checked. Both mutations were applied by hand to confirm they now fail exactly two tests, and that restoring the source makes them pass.
ACT1-N9.the_run_did_not_finish: The job was cancelled at 45m18s after testing roughly twenty of eighty-eight mutants. The remaining mutants are UNTESTED, and that is not evidence of their absence. The check is informational and structurally times out on a diff this size; earlier runs on smaller diffs completed in 6-32 minutes.
ACT1-N9.scored: The third unforecast finding to come from a gate rather than a reviewer, and the most interesting: it is the failure mode of the previous finding's fix.

ACT1-N10.title: `attests_to_its_key` was unjustified surface, and a complete mutation pass is what proved it.
ACT1-N10.observed: The full 88-mutant pass (32 min local, against CI's ~20 in 45) left two survivors. One replaced the entire body of `MeasurementRequest::attests_to_its_key` with `Ok(())` and nothing noticed.
ACT1-N10.why_nothing_noticed: It cannot fail. `MeasurementRequest::of` is the only constructor, so an in-process request that would refuse its own attestation cannot be built. Its error arms were exactly the eight unreachable lines ACT1-N8 recorded, and a grep confirmed the method had ZERO production callers — only two test assertions.
ACT1-N10.the_criterion_applied: The right response to a survivor is not automatically 'add a test'. Where the survivor sits on API with no consumer, it is evidence of unnecessary surface. Same disposition as the unused `From<MeasurementRefusal>` in ACT1-N8: deleted, not covered.
ACT1-N10.what_was_kept: `derived_key` stays. It is the load-bearing primitive — it re-derives the whole four-part key from the request alone, with no arguments — and the two tests now compare it against `key()` directly, which is what the deleted method did in one line.
ACT1-N10.the_intent_is_not_lost: The comparison belongs to whichever transition first lets a request cross a trust boundary — serde, a queue, a remote executor. It should arrive then, WITH the test that can fail it. That is recorded in the OPT-6 forecast rather than left as dead code here.
ACT1-N10.lineage: ACT1-N8 said these arms were kept for a future caller and were 'likely stage 6's problem'. Subsequent review narrowed that: they are load-bearing only if the REQUEST travels, and if stage 6 keeps the shape `in-process request -> executor -> immutable artifact -> transport -> ingest`, it is the ARTIFACT that needs hostile round-trip tests. The complete mutation pass then settled it: no consumer today, so delete. Recorded as three steps rather than rewritten into one, because how the boundary became sharper is the useful part.

ACT1-N11.title: Mutation testing reports the INACTIVE arm of every `#[cfg]`-split function as MISSED, in every configuration.
ACT1-N11.observed: The second survivor was `TeacherForcedExecutor::execute -> Ok(Default::default())` at teacher_forced.rs:155 — inside the `#[cfg(all(feature = "gpu", target_os = "macos"))]` arm, which the default-feature test build does not compile. Re-running the same file under `--features gpu` gave the mirror image.

the_matrix.note: 155 is the gpu arm, 188 the non-gpu arm. In each configuration the LIVE arm is caught or unviable and the DEAD arm is inert.

ACT1-N11.the_tell: `Observed` does not derive `Default`, so `Ok(Default::default())` CANNOT COMPILE where that arm is live — which is exactly why it comes back unviable under `--features gpu`. It was only ever 'viable' because cfg'd-out source is never type-checked. There is no configuration in which line 155 is a genuine survivor.
ACT1-N11.the_general_property: This is not about this function. For ANY `#[cfg]`-split function in this workspace, a single mutation run will report the inactive arm as MISSED regardless of test quality, because the mutation is textual and the code is not compiled. A cfg-split function can never score clean in one run.
ACT1-N11.consequence_for_the_instrument: It compounds the blind spot ACT1-N7 named. The Metal arm of the only registered executor is invisible to mutation testing in every configuration CI runs: the ubuntu leg has it cfg'd out, and the macos-14 leg is scoped to `-p larql-compute-metal` and never sees this file. Not a test gap — an instrument gap, and one that a reader of a green mutation run would not suspect.
ACT1-N11.not_fixed_here: Both this and the 45-minute cap are instrument debt and belong to a CI transition of their own, not to a rung about actuation. Recorded so that transition starts from measured facts rather than from an impression.

design_decisions_worth_recording.construct_or_refuse_rather_than_a_check_: `MeasurementRequest` has private fields and no field constructor. A `validate()` a caller may forget to call is not an invariant; the only way to hold one is `of`, which resolves the map and compares. `attests_to_its_key` exists for a request that has travelled — over a queue, out of a file — and is a re-check, not the enforcement.
design_decisions_worth_recording.the_leading_route_and_not_any_route: Several realizations reach one physical state and share one experiment, so which route the request is built from cannot change what is measured. It changes which provenance the run is attributed to, so preparation takes the route the policy ranked first rather than picking one — a bridge that reordered what it was handed would be overruling the ranking layer from below.
design_decisions_worth_recording.two_doors_stated_openly: `PreparedExperiment::of(record)` is the authorised path; `MeasurementRequest::of(record, key, applied)` restates a key a caller already holds. The second is not a selection back door and could not be one — it refuses unless the map presents that key's state — but the distinction is documented rather than left for a reader to infer, because 'choosing stays the policy's business, truthfulness is this layer's' is the whole boundary.
design_decisions_worth_recording.the_label_is_derived_and_not_carried: `TeacherForcedRequest::label` is documented as the one field that is not a control. Deriving it from the key rather than carrying it keeps that true and has a side benefit worth stating: a sweep's reports become named by the experiment they measured instead of by whatever `LARQL_Q2A_LABEL` was last set to.
design_decisions_worth_recording.instructed_everywhere_performed_somewher: The non-Metal build instructs first and then refuses. The mapping is the whole content of step 5, and putting it behind the same cfg as the instrument would mean it was only ever compiled on the one machine that cannot run CI.
design_decisions_worth_recording.observed_is_deliberately_thin: It carries the key, the reading, what the run verified, and a provenance line. No verdict, no artifact identity, no physical observations, no completion status beyond the refusal type. Stage 6 should decide what a `MeasurementArtifact` must hold from what ingestion needs, not inherit a shape chosen here for convenience.
design_decisions_worth_recording.the_record_builder_moved_rather_than_bei: Two modules now need 'the record that can actually answer'. `state/tests/container.rs` already argues that one fixture beats three ideas of what a container is; the same argument applies one level up, so the priced-record builder moved from the view's tests into `state/fixtures` and both read the same one.

what_is_still_owed.stage_6: An immutable measurement artifact, and an ingestion step that asks whether it constitutes the measurement its key names before anything enters `SearchFacts`. ACT1-N3 says why that question is real and not already answered.
what_is_still_owed.stage_7: The loop. It should be small — reload, derive, execute, ingest, repeat — and contain almost no intelligence, which is the point.
what_is_still_owed.the_overlay_build: Nothing yet turns `MeasurementRequest::candidate_map` into compiled bytes. `LocatorRefusal::NotBuilt` names the map to build, which makes the gap actionable and does not close it.
what_is_still_owed.a_second_procedure: Registry DISPATCH is now witnessed: two distinct stub procedures, both registration orders, the named one running in all four combinations, and a third-procedure refusal naming both. What that does NOT earn is ACT1-N5, which stays open — two stubs prove nothing about the relationship between an instrument's declared procedure and an execution procedure. A second REAL procedure is still owed.
what_is_still_owed.a_real_run: See ACT1-N7. The Metal arm compiles and has never run; the first real actuation belongs to stage 6's evidence programme.
what_is_still_owed.mutation_instrument_debt: Two measured facts for a future CI transition. (a) The 45-minute cap: this diff's 88 mutants take ~32 minutes locally at -j 4 and did not fit CI's budget, so the job was cancelled at roughly twenty of eighty-eight; a timed-out run is visually indistinguishable from a real failure in the checks tab, though the workflow's own header already says to read it as incomplete. (b) ACT1-N11: cfg-split functions always report their inactive arm as missed, so a clean mutation score is unobtainable for them in a single run.
